verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles on the windowsill
where the cat once sat watching birds—
now just a square of paler wood.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off
but no one moves to pour it—
steam finds the window anyway.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
She rereads the letter once more,
then feeds it to the low flame—
watching what she meant to say
curl into something like smoke.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The ash cools on the hearthstone
while somewhere a phone rings twice,
unanswered—
the room keeps her secret warm a little longer.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Morning comes anyway,
indifferent as a bus schedule—
she folds yesterday's coat
into a shape that fits in the closet.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The coat sleeve still holds her shoulder's shape—
a stranger on the bus
asks if the seat beside her
is taken.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
She says no, it's free,
and slides over an inch,
leaving room for the coat
that isn't there anymore.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The stranger sits, unaware
of the small ceremony—
window fogging with two breaths now
where there used to be one.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Two breaths, and neither one
knows the other's weather—
she wipes a clear circle
just to watch the street move.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone else's stop comes too soon—
the seat cools where the coat
almost was, almost wasn't,
and the window keeps its fog awhile longer.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
She takes the whole seat now,
spreads her bag where the quiet sat,
and doesn't notice
the glass has already forgotten.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Outside, the street repeats itself—
another coat, another stop,
the bus not caring
whose warmth it carries next.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A pigeon lands where no one waits,
struts the puddle's borrowed sky,
lifts off before the light
decides which way to change.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The wire hums the tune it always hums,
someone hears their childhood in it,
someone else just hears the wire.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Rain finds the crack it always finds,
runs the same thin river down the glass,
and calls it new
because no one told it otherwise.
